title: How Pet Psychics Work
summary: Josh and Chuck explore pet psychics and animal communicators: what they claim (telepathy, clairvoyance, an unproven electromagnetic energy field tied to Jay Alan Boone's "primal cause" idea), why people consult them (after a pet's death, illness, behavior problems, lost pets), and why skeptics attribute results to cold reading. They discuss whether animals experience emotions, grief, and self-awareness, citing the 2012 Cambridge Declaration on Consciousness, and contradictory claims by pet psychics such as Sonya Fitzpatrick and Debbie McGillivray. They close with pet spending figures and listener mail correcting a joke about a University of Hertfordshire team name.

segments.title: Opening banter and Emily's pet psychic visit
segments.summary: Hosts chat about Spanish coffee and The Simpsons, then Josh reveals Emily visited a local pet psychic after their dog Lucy was put down, and Emily is now reading up on animal intuition.

segments.title: What pet psychics claim and why people visit
segments.summary: Pet psychics claim telepathy and clairvoyance, sometimes via an electromagnetic energy field. Reasons people consult them include grief, illness or end-of-life decisions, behavior problems, and lost pets. Skeptics attribute successes to luck and coincidence.

segments.title: Electromagnetic energy, Jay Allan Boone and Animal Planet's Pet Psychic
segments.summary: Pet psychics say an unproven energy field connects all things. Jay Allan Boone's book Kinship with All Life, about his bond with the German shepherd Strongheart, is described as a pet psychic touchstone. Sonya Fitzpatrick's Animal Planet show is said to have inspired many people to discover their gift.

segments.title: How a pet psychic session works
segments.summary: A typical session involves relaxing, contacting the animal's energy, and relaying answers, often without the animal present. The psychic acts as go-between, and the answers can sound like ordinary human conversation.

segments.title: Do animals have emotions, self-awareness and grief?
segments.summary: The hosts discuss whether animals feel emotions and self-awareness. They cite the 2012 Cambridge Declaration on Consciousness, which argued that the neural substrates of consciousness are not limited to the human cortex. They explain metacognition as the current dividing line, and share Josh's family's experience of their dog Buckley grieving Lucy.

segments.title: Contradictory pet psychic claims and cold reading
segments.summary: Pet psychics give conflicting accounts, such as Sonya Fitzpatrick saying animals are gossipy and Debbie McGillivray saying they are loyal. The hosts then explain cold reading tactics, including vague statements, fishing for details, and restating client information.

segments.title: Pet spending and pet-owner communication polls
segments.summary: Americans reportedly spent sixty-one billion dollars on pets, up from thirty-six billion in 2005 and seventeen billion earlier. A 2008 poll found many owners believe they understand their pets' sounds. The hosts suggest this reflects body language and proximity.

segments.title: Listener mail: Figgy Puddings
segments.summary: A listener studying at the University of Hertfordshire corrects Josh's joke team name, noting the school's team is the Hurricanes, and praises the show.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts invite listeners to search for more on the site and get in touch by Twitter, Facebook, and email. A Netflix sponsor message closes the episode.
